Logistics / Warehousing & 3PL

Clients see their stock without asking. Billing closes on time.

For contract logistics providers, e-commerce fulfillment centers, and cold-chain and bonded warehouses serving several clients. We connect ASNs, receiving, order cut-offs, client reporting and activity-based billing around your WMS, so clients get timely, accurate information and finance bills everything the contract allows.

The challenge

What makes warehousing & 3pl different.

01

Every client sends ASNs, orders and report requests in its own format, and the team re-keys or reformats them.

02

Short, excess and damaged receipts are noted on paper and reach clients too late to claim against suppliers or transporters.

03

Orders that will miss the carrier cut-off are noticed only after the truck has left.

04

Storage, handling and value-added charges are assembled at month-end from several reports, and some are never billed.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for warehousing & 3pl.

01

ASN-to-GRN tracking

ASNs from EDI, email or the portal are validated and matched to receipts, and GRN summaries with photo evidence go out as soon as receiving closes.

02

Order cut-off and SLA watch

Orders still unpicked or unpacked as the carrier cut-off approaches are flagged to the shift lead, and clients hear about breaches with a reason.

03

Scheduled client stock statements

Stock, ageing, batch and near-expiry statements go to each client on schedule, in the format they need, from one warehouse data model.

04

Activity-based billing

Storage and handling charges are calculated from WMS activity and contract rate cards, with exceptions reviewed before finance approves the invoice.

05

Client query assistant

Clients ask about receipts, stock and order status on WhatsApp or the portal and get answers from the WMS, with handover to the account manager.

Pickup, receipt & origin handlingStandard4–6 weeks

Inbound ASN-to-GRN tracking with discrepancy alerts

Match each client's advance shipping notice with the vehicle at the dock and the goods received, flag short, excess and damaged lines with photos, and send the client a GRN summary as soon as receiving closes.

Warehousing & 3PL

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Clients send ASNs as emails, spreadsheets or EDI files, and trucks arrive without appointments. Receiving teams count against printed lists, discrepancies are noted on paper, and clients learn about shortages or damage days later when stock does not show as available. Claims against suppliers and transporters then lack timely evidence.

Trigger

A client ASN arrives by EDI, API, email or the client portal, a vehicle reports at the gate, or receiving is closed for an inbound in the WMS.

How it runs

  • Read ASNs from EDI, API, email attachments or the portal, validate SKU codes, quantities, batch and expiry fields against the client's item master, and create the expected receipt in the WMS.
  • Offer dock appointment slots to the client or transporter, and alert the dock supervisor when a vehicle arrives without an ASN or appointment.
  • During receiving, compare scanned quantities, batches and expiry dates with the ASN, and capture photos of damaged cartons and broken seals in the handheld app.
  • When receiving closes, generate a GRN summary with short, excess and damaged lines and photo links, and send it to the client's nominated contacts.
  • Open a discrepancy case for each variance with an owner and deadline, and track it until the client confirms acceptance, a return or a claim.
  • Report dock-to-stock time and discrepancy rates by client, supplier and transporter for the weekly review.

Human checkpoint

The receiving supervisor confirms every discrepancy before the GRN summary is released, and the client's nominated contact decides whether to accept, return or claim against short or damaged goods. Quarantine and release of damaged or expired stock stay with the warehouse manager.

Systems it connects

  • WMS such as Unicommerce, Increff, Vinculum or SAP EWM
  • Handheld scanners and receiving app
  • Client ERP or EDI feeds
  • Gate and dock appointment register

Data & consent

Mostly business data about goods, suppliers and vehicles, plus driver names and phone numbers at the gate. Photos are linked to the receipt and kept for the client's claim window. Each client sees only its own receipts through role-based access, and driver details are visible only to gate and dock staff.

What we deliver

  • ASN intake and validation for each client format
  • Dock appointment and arrival alerts
  • GRN summary template with photo evidence
  • Discrepancy case tracker and weekly report

How we measure it

  • Dock-to-stock time
  • GRN discrepancy rate by supplier
  • GRN summaries sent within the agreed time
  • Inbound vehicles without an ASN

In transit, at hubs & at customsAdvanced6–8 weeks

Proactive delay and SLA breach alerts with customer updates

Watch every shipment and warehouse order against its promised date or SLA, flag delays, stuck consignments, missed cut-offs and free-time risks early, give each exception an owner, and tell the customer before they have to ask.

Courier & last-mile delivery · Freight forwarding & customs · Warehousing & 3PL · Fleet & road transport

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Tracking data exists in the TMS, carrier portals, GPS dashboards and the WMS, but nobody watches all of it against what was promised. Delays surface when the customer calls, key accounts hear about rollovers or breakdowns late, warehouse orders miss the carrier cut-off unnoticed, and the same lanes, hubs and carriers fail repeatedly without data to show it.

Trigger

A milestone is missed or late against plan, the ETA moves past the promised date, a shipment shows no scan or GPS movement beyond the agreed limit, or an SLA timer nears breach.

How it runs

  • Pull milestones from the TMS, courier and carrier tracking APIs, GPS platforms, WMS order status and shipping line or airline feeds into one timeline with the promised date and SLA.
  • Run rules for missed pickups, no-movement, stuck-at-hub, ETA slippage, vessel rollovers, free-time expiry and warehouse orders not packed before the carrier cut-off, tuned per lane, service and client.
  • Create an exception with an owner, reason code and deadline in the control-tower queue, and alert the owner in Slack.
  • Send the consignee or shipper an approved WhatsApp, SMS or email update with the revised ETA; for key accounts, the account manager approves the message first.
  • Escalate exceptions still open near the SLA limit to the branch or operations head.
  • Report exceptions, causes and SLA performance by lane, hub, carrier and client for the weekly review.

Human checkpoint

Control-tower executives own every exception, confirm the reason before messages go to key accounts, and decide rerouting, upgrades and any cost or claim commitment. Customers are never promised compensation by an automated message.

Data & consent

Uses shipment details and consignee names, phone numbers and addresses only for delivery updates. Messages follow the consent records and opt-outs held for each contact and never include promotions. Location history is kept for the agreed claim window, and customers see only their own shipments.

  • SLA and root-cause dashboard

How we measure it

  • On-time delivery against promise
  • Exceptions flagged before the customer contacts you
  • Exception resolution time
  • Where-is-my-shipment contacts per thousand shipments

In transit, at hubs & at customsAdvanced5–7 weeks

Tracking-grounded support assistant on WhatsApp and web

Answer where-is-my-shipment, delivery slot, document and stock questions on WhatsApp and web chat from live tracking and WMS data, and hand over to an agent with full context whenever a person is needed.

Courier & last-mile delivery · Freight forwarding & customs · Warehousing & 3PL

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Support teams spend much of the day reading tracking screens back to customers. Consignees ask about deliveries, importers about clearance and 3PL clients about receipts and orders. After hours nobody answers, and general chatbots that guess instead of checking the data create more calls than they save.

Trigger

A consignee, shipper or client sends a message on WhatsApp or web chat, or replies to a tracking notification.

How it runs

  • Identify the shipment or order from the AWB, booking, container or order number, and verify the requester through the registered phone number or a one-time code before sharing details.
  • Retrieve live status from the TMS, tracking APIs or WMS, and answer only from that data and the approved FAQ and service policies.
  • Handle routine requests such as a delivery slot, an address landmark or a document copy within the rules set for each customer.
  • Hand over to an agent with the conversation, shipment data and a suggested next step when the request involves a claim, damage, a refund, an address change outside the rules or an unhappy customer.
  • Log every conversation with intent and outcome, and review a weekly sample of answers for accuracy.

Human checkpoint

Support agents handle claims, damage reports, refunds, complaints and any change to delivery terms. The assistant states only what the data shows, says so when it does not know, and sends low-confidence answers to an agent.

Shares shipment details only after verifying the requester, and shows masked addresses and phone numbers. Conversations are kept for the agreed support retention period. Model APIs are configured so customer conversations are not used for model training, and access to logs is limited to support leads.

  • Requester verification flow
  • Agent handover with context
  • Approved knowledge base and policies
  • Weekly accuracy and intent report

How we measure it

  • Agent handover rate
  • Answer accuracy in weekly samples
  • First response time after hours

Billing, settlement & reviewStandard4–6 weeks

Client stock statements and activity-based 3PL billing

Send each 3PL client scheduled stock, ageing and near-expiry statements from the WMS, and build monthly invoices from storage, handling and value-added activity under each contract, with exceptions reviewed before finance approves.

Warehousing & 3PL

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Clients ask for stock reports in their own formats, and the warehouse team builds them by hand from WMS exports. Billing for pallet storage, inbound and outbound handling, kitting, relabeling and returns is assembled at month-end from several reports, charges are missed or disputed, and invoices go out late.

Trigger

A client's scheduled report time, month-end close, or an ad hoc statement request from a client through the portal.

How it runs

  • Pull daily inventory snapshots and inbound, outbound, returns and value-added service logs for each client from the WMS into a warehouse data model.
  • Send scheduled stock statements with ageing, batch, near-expiry, damaged and quarantined lines to each client's nominated contacts or portal.
  • Calculate storage by pallet, bin or area per day and handling charges from each contract rate card, including minimum commitments and special rates.
  • List exceptions such as activities without a rate, unusual volumes or stock held in quarantine beyond the agreed limit, and send them to the account manager.
  • Create the draft invoice with an activity annexure for the finance controller to approve, then send both to the client.

Human checkpoint

The account manager reviews exceptions and rate questions, and the finance controller approves every invoice and credit note. Decisions on near-expiry and quarantined stock, such as liquidation, return or destruction, belong to the client and are recorded against their nominated contact.

  • Scheduled stock and expiry statements

  • Billing cycle time after month-end
  • Billing disputes per invoice
